headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line while the crowd reads Greed and ETF desks keep buying
paragraphs: Start with regime, because it settles the argument before anything else matters: all seven majors here, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, ADA, sit below their 200-day moving averages, and none shows a golden cross. That's a market still under its long-term trendline across the board, not a split verdict. BTC itself is 49.0% off its 12-month high of $124,773.51, trading at $63,653.85, down 0.34% on the day, down 1.59% over seven days, and down 2.97% over thirty. There's no reading where BTC's month is positive: the number says down, so down is what it is.

Momentum is where it gets interesting, because it's not confirming the trend, it's resting inside it. BTC's RSI-14 sits at 47.4, dead center, no oversold, no overbought, and its MACD is below signal, consistent with the soft 30-day drift. ETH tells a different story: RSI 56.3, firmer, and it's actually up 1.81% over seven days and up 6.36% over thirty even while remaining below its 200-day and 60.6% off its own high. That's a divergence worth naming: ETH is recovering in the short window while still structurally under trend, a bounce inside a downtrend rather than a trend reversal. BNB and DOGE show MACD above signal despite sitting below their 200-day lines too, small green shoots in an otherwise gray tape.

Positioning adds texture rather than alarm. BTC funding on OKX is 0.0012% per 8h (1.3% annualized), about as cheap as leverage gets, long/short ratio near flat at 1.03, and open interest of $2.19B. That's not a crowded trade. ETH funding runs hotter at 8.4% annualized with a 1.12 long/short tilt. The real crowding shows up further out the risk curve: DOGE's long/short ratio is 3.93 with 11% annualized funding, and SOL sits at 1.76 with the same 11% funding, both signs of a leveraged long crowd paying up to stay in the boat. Liquidations lean short-side heavy for BTC (shorts took $10.03M against $6.12M in longs over 13 hours) and short-heavy for DOGE too, meaning the squeezes recently have been catching bears, not bulls.

Flows are the part that doesn't match the sleepy price action. On 20 Aug, BTC spot ETFs took in a net $42.2M, and the last five sessions netted $990M with four of those days pointing the same direction, a real and current bid from traditional finance. ETH ETFs added a smaller $2.8M on the day but $291.9M over five sessions, same four-day consistency. Whale wallets echo this: $181.4M net left exchanges in the last 24 hours, split $113.9M BTC and $67.5M ETH, almost entirely from Binance. Zoom out to the weekly ledger and the picture is choppier: three of the last four weeks show net outflows from exchanges (Jul 30: $1,289M, Aug 06: $747M, Aug 20: $100M) but the week ending Aug 13 flipped hard onto exchanges at $813M. So the coin-moves-to-cold-storage story is real this week and has been dominant lately, but it is not an unbroken line.

Sentiment sits at 62, Greed, near the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 62. That's the tension: the crowd feels good, ETF desks are buying, whales are pulling coin off exchanges, and yet every major asset is still below its 200-day average with BTC down on the month. Money and mood agree on direction here, both leaning constructive, but the chart underneath hasn't confirmed it with a trend reclaim. Stablecoin float, the dry powder gauge, is essentially flat at $307.2B, down just 0.21% over 30 days, meaning the sidelined cash pile isn't growing or shrinking much either way.

What to watch: whether BTC and ETH can close back above their 200-day lines, whether the five-session ETF net flow keeps its same-direction streak going or breaks it, and whether the weekly whale flow reverts to onto-exchanges the way it did the week ending Aug 13. Any of those flipping would be the tell that this week's off-exchange, buy-the-dip posture was the exception rather than the pattern.
